title: The Star That Is Slowly Eating Its Own Planets — We Can See It
hook: A star 300 light-years away is consuming its own children, and astronomers caught it in the act.
why_this_can_go_viral: Graphic stellar cannibalism triggers the 'could it happen to Earth?' fear loop, and the visual of a planet being shredded is inherently shocking.

title: The Asteroid That Passed Closer Than GPS — And We Found It After
hook: A city-killer asteroid slipped through our satellite belt, and NASA only spotted it 5 hours later.
why_this_can_go_viral: Near-miss stories create visceral 'we almost died without knowing' fear, and the failure of detection systems feels like a cover-up or blind spot.

title: The Dead Satellite That Sent a Threat — It's Still Orbiting
hook: A satellite that stopped operating in 2012 suddenly transmitted a message that spooked the control room.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'dead thing comes back to life' trope is universally creepy, and the idea of a satellite turning hostile taps into AI paranoia.

title: The Secret Nuclear-Powered Satellite That Fell — And They Never Found It
hook: A Soviet satellite with a nuclear reactor fell to Earth in 1978, and the radioactive core was never recovered.
why_this_can_go_viral: Lost nuclear material + space cover-up = explosive viral combo. The mystery of where the core landed fuels conspiracy theories.

title: The Supernova That Will Hit Us With Radiation — We Know the Date
hook: A nearby star is about to go supernova, and the radiation pulse will hit Earth within a decade — scientists just don't tell you which one.
why_this_can_go_viral: Imminent doom stories with a specific time frame create urgency. The 'they don't tell you' angle adds a layer of suppression paranoia.

title: The Black Hole That Is Wandering Through Our Galaxy Alone
hook: A rogue black hole is drifting through the Milky Way, invisible, and could swallow everything in its path.
why_this_can_go_viral: An invisible, unstoppable predator roaming our galaxy is pure horror. The 'could it come for us?' question keeps viewers watching.

title: The Dark Matter Stream That Just Hit Earth — You Didn't Feel It
hook: A river of invisible dark matter is passing through your body right now, and scientists measured its arrival.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'it's happening to you right now' framing is highly personal and eerie. Dark matter feels spooky because it's undetectable but everywhere.

title: The Great Silence — There Is a Wall Around the Solar System
hook: Every signal we send out hits a point where it stops — something is absorbing our messages before they reach the stars.
why_this_can_go_viral: The terrifying idea that we are trapped or blocked by an unknown force creates a massive curiosity gap — and it flips the Fermi paradox into a horror story.

title: The Meteorite That Had a Microchip Inside — Dated Before Earth
hook: A rock from space contained a structure that looks man-made, and it's older than our planet.
why_this_can_go_viral: This is the ultimate 'we are not first' discovery. The microchip angle triggers AI and ancient alien conspiracies in one hit.

title: The Star That Went Supernova — Then Left a Structure Behind
hook: After a star exploded, Hubble spotted something geometric where the star used to be — and it's still there.
why_this_can_go_viral: Geometry in space suggests intelligence. The 'structure left behind' trope is pure cosmic archaeology mystery.

title: The Antarctic Ice That Holds a Record of a Space Bombardment
hook: Deep in the ice, scientists found a layer of debris from a cosmic event — and it's not from any known asteroid.
why_this_can_go_viral: Hidden extinction evidence buried in ice feels like a forbidden secret — and 'unknown object' leaves room for wild theories.

title: The Secret Chinese Space Program That Detected a Gravity Anomaly
hook: China's classified satellite network found a gravitational distortion near the Moon — and they're not sharing the data.
why_this_can_go_viral: International space secrecy combined with lunar mystery — viewers love the 'they are hiding something big' narrative.

title: The Comet That Is Made of Something That Shouldn't Exist in Nature
hook: A comet's composition includes a molecule that can only be created artificially — and it's coming closer every year.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'it's not natural' reveal is the ultimate curiosity hook. Viewers will immediately speculate it's a derelict alien ship or weapon.

title: The Galaxy That Is Being Erased — From the Inside Out
hook: A galaxy 1 billion light-years away is losing its stars one by one, as if something is consuming it systematically.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'something is eating the universe' narrative is terrifying and visually dramatic. It feels like a slow-motion apocalypse.

title: The Asteroid That Has a Twin — Orbiting Opposite Directions
hook: Two identical asteroids are locked in a dance around the Sun, one going forward, one backward — and they shouldn't exist together.
why_this_can_go_viral: Mirror pairs in nature feel unnatural — viewers will ask if they are fragments of something bigger or artificial.

title: The Radiation Belt That Is Getting Stronger — And It's Man-Made
hook: Earth's Van Allen belts are intensifying due to something we did in space — and it's trapping more deadly particles.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea that we accidentally made our planet more dangerous is both guilt-inducing and terrifying — it feels like slow self-destruction.

title: The Fermi Paradox Answer: They Are Watching — And Waiting for Us to Fail
hook: A new theory says alien civilizations are out there, but they're in hiding, observing us like an endangered species.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'we are being watched' trope is endlessly viral. Adding 'waiting for us to fail' turns it into a grim reality show where we are the main characters.

title: The Planet That Orbits Nothing — A Frozen Wanderer
hook: A rogue planet drifts alone in the void, and it has a faint glow — heat from a core that should have frozen long ago.
why_this_can_go_viral: A planet that defies physics with unexplained heat feels haunted. The loneliest object in the universe resonates emotionally.

title: The Gamma Ray Burst That Almost Hit — And Came From a Star We Can't See
hook: A massive gamma ray burst erupted from a point in the sky where there is no star — we have no idea what it was.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'invisible threat' is more terrifying than a visible one — viewers will immediately think of stealth weapons or hidden intelligence.

title: The Moon That Has a Metal Ring Orbiting It — Perfectly Circular
hook: A tiny moon in the outer solar system is surrounded by a ring that is mathematically perfect — and it shouldn't be stable.
why_this_can_go_viral: Perfect geometry in space implies design. The 'artificial ring' angle will trigger ancient astronaut theories instantly.

title: The Secret Cold War Plan to Nuke the Moon — It Almost Happened
hook: In the 1950s, the US military had a classified project to detonate a nuclear bomb on the Moon — the code name was A119.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'we almost did something insane' story is always viral. The Moon nuke plan is dark, absurd, and reveals how reckless governments were.

title: The Cosmic Web — We Found the Skeleton of the Universe
hook: An invisible network of dark matter filaments connects all galaxies — and we just mapped it for the first time.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'we live in a giant neural network' visual is mind-blowing and shareable. It makes the universe feel like a living organism.
